name: OrBIT
question: Does weekly percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation reduce overactive bladder symptoms as well as extended-release tolterodine?

arms.label: Percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (Urgent PC) weekly for 12 weeks
extended-release tolterodine 4 mg daily for 12 weeks

design.population: 100 adults with overactive bladder and urinary frequency (94 women), mean age about 58 years, at United States centers.
design.locator: abstract; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00448175 (enrollment, arm sizes, eligibility, baseline characteristics)

verdictNote: The 20% noninferiority margin was not met (P = 0.44); patient-rated improvement favored PTNS.
takeaway: Among 100 adults with OAB randomized to weekly PTNS or extended-release tolterodine, mean daily voids fell by 2.4 and 2.5 at 12 weeks (41 and 43 diaries); PTNS did not meet its noninferiority margin (P = 0.44). Patient-rated cure or improvement was 35/44 versus 23/42.

reports.label: 12-week randomized report
reports.citation: Peters KM, MacDiarmid SA, Wooldridge LS, et al. Randomized trial of percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation versus extended-release tolterodine: results from the overactive bladder innovative therapy trial. *J Urol.* 2009;182(3):1055-1061.

results.measure: Mean (SD) change in voids per day from baseline to 12 weeks
results.note: Values and P from the AUA/SUFU 2024 guideline summary of the trial; the registry reports the same means with 41 and 43 completers. The abstract states that frequency improved similarly in both groups.
results.locator: AUA/SUFU 2024 guideline p32; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00448175 primary outcome

results.measure: Mean (SD) change in episodes per day from baseline to 12 weeks
results.note: Values from the AUA/SUFU 2024 guideline summary; P not reported there. The abstract reports similar improvement in both groups.

results.measure: Share of subjects reporting cure or improvement at 12 weeks
results.note: Subject GRA at 12 weeks among evaluated respondents.

results.measure: Investigator assessment of cure or improvement at 12 weeks
results.note: The abstract describes investigator assessments as similar to the subject assessments but not statistically significant; percentages are not given.

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.note: The abstract also reports no device malfunctions.

values.ctl: Extended-release tolterodine initially 4 mg daily for 12 weeks; two participants reduced to 2 mg daily for intolerance

delivery.label: Completed the 12-week phase
delivery.note: Six and seven participants did not complete treatment; 41 PTNS and 43 tolterodine completers returned voiding diaries.

reports.label: 12-month PTNS extension
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed print date, January 2010 issue
reports.citation: MacDiarmid SA, Peters KM, Shobeiri SA, et al. Long-term durability of percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation for the treatment of overactive bladder. *J Urol.* 2010;183(1):234-240.
reports.followUp: 12 months from baseline in PTNS responders

results.measure: Share of initial PTNS responders reporting sustained improvement from baseline at 6 and 12 months
results.note: In the uncontrolled extension, 33 of 35 initial responders continued PTNS; GRA was assessed in 32 at 6 months and 25 at 12 months.

delivery.note: Of 44 PTNS treatment completers, 35 responded at 12 weeks, 33 continued PTNS and 25 completed 12 months.
